newsitem.title: UK: CU leads British insurance shares higher.
newsitem.headline: CU leads British insurance shares higher.

text.p: Blue-chip British insurance shares were in the vanguard of the market's advance on Tuesday as investors returned to the sector after its period of recent weakness, dealers said.
The life assurance sector got an additional boost from annual results from Sun Life & Provincial Holdings Plc, which prompted a "buy" rating from analysts at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson.
"The sector was looking oversold and people are picking up stock again," one market-maker said.
Commercial Union Plc was up 22-1/2p to 662-1/2 by 1433 GMT, while General Accident Plc climbed 24-1/2p to 807-1/2.
Royal & Sun Alliance Insurance Group Plc rose 10p to 440 on volume of 10.1 million shares and Guardian Royal Exchange Plc firmed 5-1/2p to 276.
Among life stocks, Sun Life climbed 16p to 295-1/2 after announcing a three percent rise in profits in 1996.
Legal & General Group Plc rose 3-1/2p to 387-1/2 and United Assurance Plc gained 6-1/2p to 496-1/2.
